# Upgrading SDKs generated by perseid 0.6

perseid writes an SDK's skeleton (manifest, README, error types) once, then leaves it to you. The
0.7 runtime needs a few changes to skeletons written by 0.6: `perseid generate` lists the ones your
SDKs miss and stops before writing anything. When it says to delete a file, move your changes
aside, delete it, and run `perseid generate` again: it writes the current one.

| Language | Skeleton change |
|---|---|
| Rust | `Cargo.toml`: replace `http1 = { package = "http", ... }` by `http = "1"`. `src/error.rs`: `http1::` becomes `http::` |
| Go | `go.mod`: `go 1.23` or later. `errors.go`: add `Body any` to `APIError` |
| Python | `<package>/errors.py`: delete it |
| Java | `exceptions/ApiException.java`: delete it |
| C# | `ApiException.cs`: delete it. With `dependency_injection`, reference `Microsoft.Extensions.Http` in the `.csproj` |
| TypeScript | none. `src/util.ts` is no longer used and can go |

New skeleton files (a README, Go's `doc.go`) are not added to existing SDKs: copy them from a fresh
`perseid generate --out` if you want them.

## API changes your users will see

Old names stay as deprecated aliases where noted, so most code keeps compiling with warnings.

- **Every language**: list methods return pages that also iterate every item; streams with a
  declared event schema yield models; raw responses, unknown properties and
  `<PREFIX>_API_KEY`/`<PREFIX>_BASE_URL` are new (see [features](features.md)). A 429 on a
  non-idempotent request without an `Idempotency-Key` is no longer retried. An operation whose
  spec also declares a bodiless 2xx returns "no value" for it (`undefined`, `None`, `nil`,
  `Option`, `Optional`, `T?`) instead of failing to decode.
- **TypeScript**: errors are `<Client>Error` subclasses (`APIError`, `APIConnectionError`...);
  `ApiError`, `ApiException` and `ApiTimeoutError` stay as aliases. `list()` returns a
  `PagePromise`, `listIter()` stays.
- **Python**: `Client(api_key=..., base_url=..., timeout=..., max_retries=...)`; `token=` and
  `httpx_client=` still work with a warning. Errors follow `APIError` / `APIStatusError` /
  `APIConnectionError`, with the 0.6 names as aliases. `list()` returns a page, `list_iter()` stays.
- **Go**: required query and header parameters are positional; options structs are always
  pointers. `Set`/`Null` stay as deprecated wrappers of `NewNullable`/`ExplicitNull`, and
  `IsNull()` is false on a nil `*Nullable`. Union discriminators have their own string type. An
  existing SDK keeps its package name.
- **Rust**: `Client::builder()` and `from_env()`; options structs with required parameters are
  built with `new(...)`. Calls return a `Call` future (`.await` as before, `.with_response()`).
  `Paginator` owns its client.
- **Java**: models are immutable with builders, optional getters return `Optional`; required
  parameters are positional; `widgets()` replaces `getWidgets()` (kept, deprecated);
  `client.async()` returns `CompletableFuture`s. The client is `AutoCloseable`.
- **C#**: model properties are `init`; `*AutoPagingAsync()` replaces `*IterAsync()` (kept,
  obsolete); `MaxRetries` replaces `NumRetries` (kept, obsolete); network failures throw
  `ApiConnectionException` and timeouts `ApiTimeoutException`, both `<Client>Exception`s.
